SymbolicEssence.ArchetypalFunction: To embody primordial light and celestial observation; father of sun, moon, and dawn.
SymbolicEssence.SymbolicCore: The first light, the watchful heights, progenitor of celestial bodies.

MythicAppearances: Father of Helios, Selene, and Eos
Pillar of the East in cosmology
CulturalContext.ReligiousOrRitualUse: Limited direct worship; honored as progenitor of light; one of the four pillars holding up the sky.
CulturalContext.HistoricalEvolution: Pre-Olympian light deity; functions absorbed by Apollo and Helios; name became poetic epithet for the sun.

SymbolicRepresentation.ImageryNotes: Depicted as radiant titan of great height, often with solar imagery; holding up the eastern corner of the sky.
SymbolicRepresentation.PoeticInvocation: Lord of the heights, father of all light, pillar that holds the dawn.
SymbolicRepresentation.DreamForm: A towering figure of pure light standing at the edge of the world, holding up the sky

MetaIntegration.RitualFunction: Invoked for clarity, illumination, and cosmic awareness; honored at dawn.
AIPromptSeeds: The father of light who watches from the heights as his children illuminate the world.
The pillar that holds up heaven, radiant and eternal.
NarrativeHooks: The watchful presence that sees all
The progenitor whose children outshine him
